criteria: Down 20%+ over 1 month, market cap over $1B, RSI under 45, a real recent earnings miss (or swing to a loss), gross margin still positive and revenue not collapsing (down under 25% YoY, not declining 3+ of the last 4 quarters), excludes banks, pharma, and biotech. Ranked by Reset Score (0 to 100), recomputed daily from live price/RSI against the original earnings shock and leadership finding: earnings shock size, price drop severity, RSI, and a confirmed recent leadership change as a bonus signal. Cards persist day to day once listed and only drop off if the price moves 15%+ from where it was first flagged.
disclaimer: Informational screener only, not investment advice. Data from live market feed. Not a recommendation to buy or sell any security.

cards.name: Nayax
cards.why: Runs a global payments and commerce platform. Swung from an expected profit to an outright loss this quarter, one of the sharpest misses in this group, and shares are down 27% since. No leadership change surfaced in our research; this looks like an operational reset standing on its own.

cards.name: Playtika
cards.why: Develops and operates mobile games. CFO Craig Abrahams is departing (an acting CFO steps in) right on top of a quarter that missed estimates by 30% amid a $206M annual loss, a leadership shakeup landing on the worst print in a while, with shares down 39%.

cards.name: Hut 8 Corp
cards.why: Runs data centers for AI and bitcoin mining. The second quarter swung to a much deeper loss than expected, one of the sharpest misses in this group, with shares down 22% since. No leadership change surfaced in our research; this looks like an operational reset on its own, while revenue has kept growing.

cards.name: BillionToOne
cards.why: Makes molecular diagnostics tests. Missed estimates by 38% this quarter, and shares are down 30% since. No confirmed leadership change turned up in our research; this reads as a large isolated miss rather than a documented change in leadership.

cards.name: ATS Corporation
cards.why: Runs automated manufacturing and assembly systems. New CEO Doug Wright took over in January 2026 after predecessor Andrew Hider's abrupt departure in the middle of 2025, and the first quarter fully under him missed estimates by 14%, a classic leadership reset, with shares down 25% since.

cards.name: Trade Desk
cards.why: Runs a programmatic ad buying platform. Its finance seat has turned over three times in under a year: a CFO out after 6 months, an interim, now a third hire in July, and the latest quarter missed estimates by 8%, with shares down 25% since.
